module_title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) vs. IPC: Foundational Concepts
introduction: This foundational level introduces the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which officially replaced the colonial-era Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) on July 1, 2024. It covers the structural overhaul, the re-prioritization of offenses, and the newly introduced punishments.

core_concepts.title: Structural Overhaul and Prioritization
core_concepts.description:
The IPC was drafted by Lord Macaulay in 1860. The BNS modernizes and streamlines it.
- Reduction in Sections: The IPC had 511 sections; the BNS has 358 sections.
- Shift in Priorities: The IPC prioritized offenses against the State (Treason, Rebellion) over individuals. The BNS flips this. Chapter V of BNS prioritizes 'Crimes Against Women and Children', followed by 'Offenses against the Human Body', pushing 'Offenses against the State' to Chapter VII.

core_concepts.title: New Form of Punishment: Community Service (Section 4)
core_concepts.description:
Under Section 53 of the IPC, punishments included Death, Life Imprisonment, Rigorous/Simple Imprisonment, Forfeiture of Property, and Fine.
- BNS Addition: Section 4(f) of the BNS officially introduces 'Community Service' as a formal legal punishment for petty offenses (like minor theft, defamation, or public intoxication) to promote restorative justice and reduce prison overcrowding.

core_concepts.title: Complete Omissions from the Penal Code
core_concepts.description:
The BNS completely removes certain offenses that were deemed obsolete or unconstitutional:
1. Adultery (Sec 497 IPC) - Already struck down by the Supreme Court in 'Joseph Shine v. Union of India'.
2. Unnatural Offenses (Sec 377 IPC) - Partially struck down in 'Navtej Johar'. The BNS completely omits 377, creating a legal vacuum regarding non-consensual acts on men/transgender individuals or animals.
3. Thug (Sec 310 IPC) - Removed as an obsolete colonial provision.

core_concepts.title: Section Mapping (The Shift of Famous IPC Sections)
core_concepts.description:
Examiners will heavily test the new section numbers for famous crimes:
- Murder: IPC 302 is now BNS 103.
- Rape: IPC 376 is now BNS 63.
- Cheating (420): IPC 420 is now BNS 318.
- Defamation: IPC 499/500 is now BNS 356.

important_entities.name: Deceitful Promise to Marry (Section 69 BNS)
important_entities.significance: Previously, cases where a man had sexual intercourse on a false promise to marry were prosecuted under Rape (IPC 376). BNS Section 69 creates a specific, separate offense for sexual intercourse by employing 'deceitful means' (false promise of employment, promotion, or marriage without intention to fulfill it). It is punished with up to 10 years imprisonment, distinguishing it legally from rape.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly tested exam trap: Statements claiming 'Sedition has been completely abolished in India under BNS.' This is technically FALSE. While the *word* 'Sedition' and IPC Section 124A have been deleted, the *crime* has been reintroduced with a wider scope under BNS Section 152 as 'Acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 103 is the new 302 (Murder); 318 is the new 420 (Cheating)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorize the 'New 420' (318) and 'New 302' (103) as they are the most culturally ingrained sections that have shifted.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question asks 'Which newly introduced punishment in BNS 2023 focuses on restorative justice for petty crimes?', unconditionally select **Community Service**.
